beats.narration_text: Hej — this is Liam, in for Bear. The ask, rebuilt for the camera: three simple 3D assets for Jelly Hop, where a jelly cube dodges forks on a dinner table. This prompt is an illustrative reconstruction. Kiran's real prompt and screenshots come next.

beats.act: the three assets and why the game needs each
beats.narration_text: Why each one. The fork is the hazard: it stabs down from above, so the jelly has to time its jumps. The dessert dome is the goal at the end of the level. The biscuit is a stepping stone to land on, planned for future levels. Every size is set against the half-metre jelly: the fork is three jellies tall.

beats.narration_text: Kiran's own screenshot: the fork prompt to Claude Code. It names Walker's loop and points at the brief, then repeats its numbers: half a metre wide, one and a half tall, six boxes, a budget of a hundred triangles. Then: propose the steps; do not build yet. No asset libraries, no generators.

props.title: The Prompt: Brief First, Plan Before Building
props.status: Kiran's screenshot 23 · Claude Code in Terminal

beats.narration_text: What it built, again Kiran's screenshot. Claude's plan: four prongs, a head and a handle, six boxes, all five centimetres deep. Kiran accepted it. The status bar reads Tris seventy-two, under the budget of a hundred, and Kiran checked that the fork points down with its tips at the origin.

props.title: What It Built: Six Boxes, 72 Triangles

beats.narration_text: The hand edit. In Material Preview the dome looked washed out: the cover nearly white-lavender, the cherry salmon. Kiran opened the Material tab and raised the cover's saturation from about point one eight to point four five, then darkened the cherry and warmed the cream. One slip on the way: a value went into the wrong field and the cherry turned blue, so Kiran restored the original before redoing it.

beats.narration_text: Now Godot. The showcase scene is a small text file. Each asset is an instance of its exported glb, set side by side: the platform at minus two point five, the dome at the origin, the fork at one point five. And a half-metre cube at three: a size reference for the jelly, not an asset.

beats.narration_text: The check. Line seven: expected values come from the brief, never from the files checked. Blender is Z-up and Godot is Y-up, so each row is the brief turned on its side: the fork's height, one and a half, moves to the middle. Each row also carries the budget and the count Kiran read in Blender.

props.title: The Check: The Brief in Godot’s Axes
props.code:
# Expected values come from the brief (Blender X, Y, Z -> Godot X, Z, Y), never from the files checked.
const ASSETS := [
	{"key": "fork", "path": "res://assets/models/fork.glb", "node": "Fork", "size": Vector3(0.5, 1.5, 0.05), "budget": 100, "blender_tris": 72},
	{"key": "dome", "path": "res://assets/models/dome.glb", "node": "Dome", "size": Vector3(1.0, 0.75, 1.0), "budget": 300, "blender_tris": 266},
	{"key": "platform", "path": "res://assets/models/platform.glb", "node": "Platform", "size": Vector3(2.0, 0.25, 1.5), "budget": 60, "blender_tris": 36},
]

beats.act: result: headless numbers beside the brief
beats.narration_text: Run headless, numbers only, beside the brief. Every size matches within a millimetre. Triangles: seventy-two, two sixty-six and thirty-six, all under budget. Each lowest point sits on the floor. Thirty-six checks, zero failures, exit code zero. Nothing is rendered, so it says nothing about colour or look.

beats.act: what Kiran checked and what remains uncertain
beats.narration_text: What Kiran checked by eye: sizes in Blender's sidebar, triangles in the status bar, the scene through its camera, and the undersides with the floor hidden. Still uncertain: with one light and no environment the shaded sides are pure black; the fork tips were not checked close up; a fresh run of the dome script brings back Claude's colours; and the placements. Read from the A2 code, the dome sits on the table, not on a final platform. Kiran has not confirmed that yet.

beats.narration_text: What Claude got wrong. Its dome colours were washed out; Kiran fixed them by hand. Its first plan had the cherry touching the cover at one point; Kiran had it sunk four centimetres in. It removed an unused material and set fake users, steps its plan never mentioned, and reported both afterwards. And it flagged its own cherry test as weak.

props.title: What Claude Got Wrong
props.treeLabel: What Claude Code got wrong → what happened next
tree: Dome colours washed out → Kiran's hand edit
Cherry touching the cover at one point → Kiran: 0.04 m in
Removed "Dots Stroke", set fake users: not in its plan → reported after
Its own cherry test is weak → flagged by Claude itself
output: Not Claude: the course `claude mcp add` command failed (Claude Code 2.1.288).

beats.narration_text: Verdict. Three assets on brief: sizes, origins, upright, under budget, and thirty-six headless checks with no failures. Uncertain: the black sides, the fork tips, the dome script's colours and the placements. Kiran wrote the brief and every number in it, approved each plan and each Blender call, made the hand edit, and did every human check. Claude Code wrote and ran the Blender code, the Godot scene and the check, and made this film; Claude chat guided Kiran and organised the notes. One next step, from the open items: decide where the dome goes, on the table or on a final platform, before these assets enter a level. Shown at revision nine four eight A B six A.
